summary: Quarterly check-in focused on preparing for expected holiday traffic spike. Discussed short-term burst capacity, Dedicated vs Hosted economics, caching and batching opportunities, security and audit needs (SOC2/KMS/SSO), and an agreed pilot to validate latency and unit cost at peak. Action items include pricing, pilot test, and sharing security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-21
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Carlos Mendes (Redwood AE); Priya Raman (Redwood SE); Maya Patel (HelioCart, Head of ML); Ethan Ross (HelioCart, Platform); Alicia Gomez (HelioCart, Finance); Samir Kahn (HelioCart, CTO)

[00:00] Carlos Mendes: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off, Maya, do you wanna start with the context for this quarter?
[00:18] Maya Patel: yeah, thanks Carlos. we have a big promo on Black Friday and homeowners, sorry, customers are expected to spike 4-6x baseline. we normally run a mix of synchronous chat and async batch generation for emails. our primary concern is latency SLOs during peaks and the cost blowout, so we wanted to align on options — Dedicated, bursts, or a hybrid.
[00:42] Ethan Ross: and to add, we've got tight compliance to meet — SOC two is in place but we need KMS integration for key rotation, and SSO via SAML for our engineers. also want audit log retention options.
[01:05] Priya Raman: totally, we see similar patterns with other retailers. quick note: when you say 4-6x, what's the tail on sequence length and how many concurrent users are you assuming?
[01:18] Maya Patel: median is about 120 tokens for chat, but there are long context cases up to 1,200 tokens for session history. concurrency peak estimate is ~1.2k concurrent active sessions; async jobs hit 5k requests per minute at batch times.
[01:36] Priya Raman: got it. that distribution matters — longer sequences will affect per-token cost and memory for KV cache. we can outline two approaches: 1) Hosted with burst capacity + autoscale rules, 2) Dedicated pool with reserved concurrency and burst lanes, or 3) hybrid routing where critical routes go to Dedicated and bulk async goes to Hosted cheaper variants.
[02:05] Samir Kahn: Alicia, how flexible is the budget? are we prepared to pay more for predictability?
[02:12] Alicia Gomez: short answer: we need a clear ROI. predictable cost for core flows is acceptable but we can't have token spend more than projected; we need guardrails. also want to see potential savings from batching and quantization.
[02:28] Carlos Mendes: perfect, we'll show a scenario spreadsheet. quick reality check — Dedicated lowers variance and gives you reserved capacity; Hosted is easiest but burst costs can spike. we can also auto-fallback to lower-cost quantized model family if Dedicated is exhausted.
[02:50] Maya Patel: what's the ops overhead to run Dedicated? we've got a small infra team.
[02:55] Priya Raman: Dedicated is managed — you get a console, autoscaling policies, and Redwood handles the runtime. you'll still need to configure routing policies and some network setup for VPC peering if you want Private. for on-prem it's more involved.
[03:14] Ethan Ross: can you remind me about private deployment vs dedicated? i thought they were the same.
[03:18] Priya Raman: they're related but different. Dedicated is Redwood-managed reserved GPUs in our environment for your tenant. Private gives you customer-controlled control plane — VPC peering, your own network egress, and optionally an on-prem package. Private is typically chosen for strict data residency or air-gapped needs.
[03:36] Maya Patel: on KMS front, we need customer-managed keys — can Redwood support HSM/KMS integration and bring-your-own-key?
[03:44] Carlos Mendes: yes, BYOK is supported for Private and Dedicated via KMS integration; we can also provide envelope encryption options. we'll share the integration checklist.
[03:52] Alicia Gomez: do you store logs with PII? we cannot have user messages retained longer than 30 days.
[03:58] Priya Raman: by default we retain logs for 90 days but we have retention policies per-tenant; we can set to 30 days and have redaction hooks. note: some analytics require de-identified traces.
[04:14] Maya Patel: ok. on performance: can Redwood do warm KV cache across sessions? our sessions are sticky but sometimes users switch devices.
[04:23] Priya Raman: we support prefix and KV cache strategies; sticky sessions help but we also do distributed KV cache warmers. caveat: cross-device warm cache depends on your session id strategy. also note that the SDK can pre-warm cache for expected prompts which helps latency.
[04:45] Ethan Ross: are there cold-start penalties if we autoscale from zero?
[04:49] Priya Raman: yes, cold starts exist — we recommend a small baseline Dedicated pool or keep a min-replicas setting to avoid cold starts for critical endpoints. Hosted has faster warmups but you trade cost predictability.
[05:05] Carlos Mendes: let's walk through a quick scenario cost run: (Carlos shares screen - reference: pricing deck) for 1.2k concurrent at 120 tokens median, with 6x peak, here's Hosted vs Dedicated with reserved baseline + burst.
[05:20] Maya Patel: (interruption) hmm that Hosted line seems lower on the spreadsheet than we expected; is that including amortized burst overhead and queuing?
[05:27] Carlos Mendes: good catch — the Hosted column assumes successful autoscale with no fallback; if you factor in fallback to higher-cost on-demand instances or SLO violations, effective cost rises. the Dedicated scenario shows a higher fixed cost but lower per-token marginal during peak.
[05:46] Alicia Gomez: and what's the penalty if SLA is missed? do you offer credits?
[05:50] Carlos Mendes: yes, enterprise customers on Dedicated can get SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; credits are applied per contract — we'll include the SLA language in the docs.
[06:01] Priya Raman: another lever: batching windows for async email jobs. increasing batch window from 1s to 10s can lower cost per request dramatically while adding small latency. for your email pipeline that's likely acceptable.
[06:17] Ethan Ross: can we do dynamic quantization for non-critical models to save costs?
[06:21] Priya Raman: yes, Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles per workload. you can route low-criticality traffic to 4-bit quantized variants and keep critical chat on fp16. there is a small quality delta we should validate with evals.
[06:33] Maya Patel: we really want to test quality impact on our prompts.
[06:36] Priya Raman: we'll include an eval harness. take sample prompts and we'll run A/B against quantized and non-quantized models; results will be in the pilot.
[06:45] Samir Kahn: ok, security question — what about audit logs and compliance for our auditors? we need exportable logs and per-token cost breakdowns by API key.
[06:56] Carlos Mendes: Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns and per-route dashboards. audit logs can be exported for the retention window you choose, and we support SAML SSO and RBAC to restrict who can access billing vs infra.
[07:12] Alicia Gomez: about billing — can you produce a forecasted spend by day for the promo week? we need to present to finance.
[07:18] Carlos Mendes: yes, if you provide traffic traces we can run a day-by-day forecast with scenarios for 2x/4x/6x surges.
[07:26] Ethan Ross: here's a technical nit — our architecture uses a CDN in front, and we do client side prompt assembly. can Redwood accept batched requests with multiple prompts per call?
[07:35] Priya Raman: absolutely, we support batching and multiplexed requests; batching strategies are configurable in the SDK and at the route level. note: extremely large batches can increase memory usage; we'll tune based on pilot results.
[07:49] Maya Patel: timeline — we need final decision by Dec 8 to sign PO and get capacity. feels tight.
[07:56] Carlos Mendes: understood — timeline works, we can prioritize the pilot this week and deliver results next week.
[08:03] Priya Raman: propose: 1) you send traffic sample, 2) Redwood runs 2-hour capacity run emulating peak, 3) we produce cost per-token and latency SLO metrics and recommended routing.
[08:14] Maya Patel: agreed. also please include a run where we simulate KV cache cold path.
[08:19] Priya Raman: yes, we'll run cold and warm cache scenarios.
[08:22] Carlos Mendes: note on blockers: network setup for Dedicated requires a short peering window; Ethan, can your infra team enable peering?
[08:30] Ethan Ross: yes, we can provision peering; will need a bit of handholding for firewall rules.
[08:35] Samir Kahn: any known service disruptions in the last quarter? we saw reports from a competitor about a regional outage, we need to understand Redwood's incident history.
[08:44] Carlos Mendes: we had one localized outage in us-west early Q3 due to a storage controller fault; impact limited to 45 minutes for affected hosts. post-incident we implemented extra replication and improved tracing — full postmortem is in the support pack we'll share.
[08:59] Maya Patel: good. also, we might need restricted data residency for EU customers in 2026; can we get a timeline for regions?
[09:06] Priya Raman: we have EU capacity in all major public regions; for Private on-prem we'd coordinate timelines. we'll include region availability in the doc.
[09:14] Alicia Gomez: can Redwood provide a fixed-price pilot option? finance prefers a capped pilot fee.
[09:20] Carlos Mendes: yes, we can do a capped pilot for the run — I'll include a fixed-fee option in the pricing email.
[09:27] Maya Patel: thanks. one tiny transcription note when you shared the spreadsheet earlier, it had an item labeled "KV cash" — just flagging that might be a mis-typo in the doc.
[09:35] Priya Raman: (laughs) yeah the transcriber loves cash. it's KV cache.
[09:38] [laughter] 
[09:45] Carlos Mendes: ok let's nail the deliverables. Priya, you'll run the pilot — confirm availability?
[09:52] Priya Raman: yes, free window on 2025-11-28 10:00-12:00 PST; will reserve it.
[09:58] Carlos Mendes: Maya/Ethan, you'll share the traffic sample and representative prompts by 11/25?
[10:03] Maya Patel: yes.
[10:05] Alicia Gomez: Alicia will check budget and confirm on 11/27.
[10:09] Carlos Mendes: i'll send Dedicated pricing and the option for capped pilot fee by Monday 11/24 along with SOC2 and security pack.
[10:16] Maya Patel: quick question on the eval harness — can we run quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets? we want noise detection and fallback to rulest-based responses if the model regresses.
[10:26] Priya Raman: yes, Redwood Optimize supports evals and regression alerts; you can tie alerts to prompt sets and trigger rollbacks or route to fallback models. we also have built-in tools for auto-A/B and can integrate with your monitoring to create incident triggers.
[10:40] Ethan Ross: what about rate limiting across routes? will that help protect us from runaway scripts?
[10:45] Priya Raman: rate limits can be token-based or request-based and applied per API key, per route, or per org. you can also set soft and hard limits.
[10:54] Samir Kahn: i want a one-page exec summary showing cost forecast, recommended deployment, and risks for Dec 8 sign-off.
[11:01] Carlos Mendes: we'll produce that; expect the one-pager with the pilot results by 11/29.
[11:07] Maya Patel: is there anything else?
[11:09] Alicia Gomez: just to confirm — the pilot will include: warm/cold cache runs, quantized vs baseline models A/B, 2-hour concurrency run, and cost breakdown by route.
[11:18] Priya Raman: correct.
[11:20] Carlos Mendes: excellent. recap of next steps and owners... (recap omitted)
[11:28] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription artifacts: speaker turns sometimes merged; acronyms occasionally mis-transcribed (Samuel for SAML, K-V cash for KV cache). timestamps are approximate.
